summary: Checked 38 factual claims in tech-spec.md; 36 confirmed in code, 2 minor anomalies found. All file paths, symbols, line-bounded code references, deploy structure, and dependency claims verified against the actual codebase. No critical mirages.

findings.claim: tech-spec Task 5 says: 'Add author_plug_filter.py to the FILES=(...) array in both deploy.sh:52 and .github/workflows/deploy.yml:132' — implying the FILES array starts at deploy.sh:52 and deploy.yml:132.
findings.actual: FILES=( opens at deploy.sh:37 and at .github/workflows/deploy.yml:117. Lines 52 and 132 happen to be the boilerplate_filter.py entries inside those arrays — the spec is using those line numbers as anchors near where the new entry should be inserted, not as the array start. Both arrays exist with the listed shape and both currently include boilerplate_filter.py exactly at those lines. Reads as confusing but not wrong: the new line would be inserted near the listed lines.
findings.fix: Reword to 'insert near deploy.sh:52 / deploy.yml:132 (next to the existing boilerplate_filter.py entry)' or refer to the FILES= start lines (37 / 117).

findings.claim: tech-spec Solution (line 15) and Architecture diagram (lines 49-52) describe a 'Google Translate fallback (per-article OR global)' path emerging from a per-article ClaudeTranscreationError.
findings.actual: news_bot._fallback_publish at lines 943-956 catches ClaudeTranscreationError and re-raises it (slot strike) — there is NO per-article Google fallback in the current code. Google fallback only fires from (a) is_fallback_active() shortcut at line 927, or (b) ClaudeOutageError degraded mode at line 1004. The convergence point at line 1006 is still correct because no Google path exists for ClaudeTranscreationError — those re-raises bypass _fallback_publish entirely and don't reach the planned variant-B insertion. Spec wording about 'per-article' Google fallback overstates the current state; the consequence for variant B's call site is unaffected.
findings.fix: Drop 'per-article' from the Google-fallback description, or note explicitly that per-article Google fallback was removed in earlier work and only the global outage-degraded path remains.
